1731: Where do you go after your shift?
1732: To the Lotus Bathhouse, in Chinatown. Hot water, nobody asks anything. It's the only luxury I've got, boss.
1733: And guess who I see there all the time? Mr. Rossi. Always wearing gloves, always talking to the old men from the Syndicate.
1734: Victor Rossi, at a Lotus Syndicate bathhouse. Worth a visit to Chinatown.
1735: The rich old guy in the expensive overcoat? Came every Thursday! Went to Itoko no Ie, right next to the mahjong parlor.
1736: Here? No, detective. Mr. Pendelton didn't like hot water.
1737: He preferred Itoko no Ie, the "cousins' house", across the alley, next to the mahjong parlor. Everyone in Chinatown knows. Nobody talks.
1738: A house of "cousins". Arthur had more secrets than patents.
1740: Welcome to Itoko no Ie, the "cousins' house", detective. Here discretion costs a lot. The police, even more.
1742: Arthur Pendelton visited Itoko no Ie every Thursday, under the name "Mr. Aurora". Two months ago, Victor Rossi paid Jade to learn which rich clients had secrets. She told him about Arthur.
